items.prompt: Tap every loose Black piece (attacked and not defended).

claims.statement: The rook on c8 and the knight on d5 are loose.
The bishop on h3 attacks the rook on c8.
The rook on d1 attacks the knight on d5.
The knight on f3 attacks the bishop on g5.
The pawn on h6 defends the bishop on g5.

hints: Follow each white piece along its lines and note which black pieces it attacks.
For each attacked black piece, ask: does any black piece protect it?
Two pieces qualify. One stands on the back rank and one in the centre.
items.explain: The bishop on h3 attacks the rook on c8 and the rook on d1 attacks the knight on d5; no black piece defends either. The bishop on g5 is attacked by the knight but the h6 pawn defends it.

items.prompt: White to move. Win the most material with one capture.

claims.statement: Bxc8 wins the rook for nothing.
Bxc8 is the engine's first choice.
Rxd5 also wins a piece, but it is clearly worse than taking the rook.

hints: Two Black pieces are loose. Which one has the higher counting value?
A rook counts 5, a knight 3.
Look at your bishop on h3: which black piece does it attack?
items.explain: Bxc8 takes a rook with nothing to recapture. Rxd5 would win a knight, but the rook on c8 could then step away. Take the loose piece with the higher counting value first.

feedback_by_move.d1d5: This also wins a piece, but the rook on c8 has the higher counting value and could escape afterwards.
feedback_by_move.f3g5: The h6 pawn recaptures: the bishop on g5 was defended.

claims.statement: Only the knight on c3 is loose.

hints: Check your own pieces too, after every opponent move.

items.explain: The bishop on b4 attacks the knight on c3, and the b-pawn has already left b2, so nothing defends the knight. Your rooks and queen are covered by each other.

items.prompt: Black to move. Win a pawn on e4 by capturing with the right piece first.

claims.statement: dxe4 followed by the knight recapture wins a pawn along the engine line.
dxe4 is the engine's first choice.

hints: Two of your pieces attack e4. Which one is cheaper?
Capture with the cheaper piece first so the defender's recapture costs it less.
The pawn takes first; the knight is kept for the second capture.
items.explain: dxe4 dxe4 Nxe4: Black's pawn goes first, White's pawn recaptures, and the knight takes the second pawn. If the knight went first it would be recaptured by a pawn and Black would lose more than it gains.

feedback_by_move.f6e4: The d3 pawn recaptures the knight: you give a knight (3) for a pawn (1).
